1	# COR-2268 workspace extraction plan
2	
3	Trail: https://entire.com/gh/entireio/-/trails/2534 (repository change #401). Full plan published in the Workspace extraction implementation plan discussion.
4	
5	Status: implementation plan; no production changes made. Baseline: merged PR #486, commit `0351e4957633761cfec0e57573877f3eabf3aff0`.
6	
7	The next bounded PR should establish `internal/cli/workspace` as the owner of workspace models, manifest operations, and cross-repo graph algorithms. Move the independent tests with those implementations. Keep command assembly and operations that depend on retrieval, privacy, providers, or daemon lifecycle in `cli` until their dependencies have explicit package boundaries.
8	
9	This is the first stage of the workspace split. It removes approximately 1,542 lines of function/type declarations and 33 independent test roots from the CLI compilation unit. It does **not** remove two minutes of test execution. The slower workspace-pattern implementation needs a subsequent extraction.
10	
11	## What the timing evidence establishes
12	
13	The completed local race run passed at this exact source tree. `TestWorkspace*` roots totaled 117.19 seconds of reported elapsed time across 142 tests. That naming group crosses several implementations:
14	
15	| Existing test file | Test roots | Sum of reported elapsed time | Placement in the next PR |
16	| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
17	| `pattern_workspace_semantic_test.go` | 6 | 67.35 s | Retain with the pattern-family implementation |
18	| `workspace_command_regression_test.go` | 15 | 29.96 s | Retain real root-command integration coverage |
19	| `workspace_pattern_failure_regression_test.go` | 4 | 8.16 s | Retain pattern publication/privacy integration coverage |
20	| `workspace_test.go` | 76 | 3.77 s | Split out the 33 independent tests listed below |
21	| `workspace_concurrency_test.go` | 5 | 0.56 s | Retain real lock/setup integration coverage |
22	
23	These are elapsed sums, not additive critical-path savings: some tests use `t.Parallel()`. The 33 initial move candidates each reported `0.00` seconds at the test log's precision. Their value is ownership, a smaller test compilation unit, and independent caching; any build-time benefit must be measured after extraction. Do not claim the earlier 117-second group as this PR's speedup.
24	
25	Evidence: `../workspace-test-weight.json`, `../merged-validation/race.log`, `../workspace-test-dependencies.json`.
26	
27	## Package ownership
28	
29	```text
30	cli assembly and feature adapters
31	  ├── entities
32	  └── workspace
33	        └── internal/base
34	
35	workspace tests ──> internal/clitest
36	```
37	
38	There must be no production or internal-test import from `workspace` back into `cli`. MCP and pattern code may consume workspace models and store operations through their existing CLI assembly. The feature package does not import those consumers.
39	
40	| Destination | Responsibility and current source |
41	| --- | --- |
42	| `internal/cli/workspace/types.go` | `workspaceManifest`, `workspaceRepo`, `workspaceRepoFreshness`, `workspaceAddResult`, `workspaceSummary`; preserve fields and JSON tags |
43	| `internal/cli/workspace/store.go` | Directory resolution, lazy legacy migration, load/write manifest, locked add, membership lock, refresh-result merge; currently distributed through `workspace.go` |
44	| `internal/cli/workspace/validate.go` | Workspace/repo-key/display-name validation, sorting, README rendering, repo-key mismatch predicate, pairing-unsafe scan predicate |
45	| `internal/cli/workspace/graph_types.go` | Contract, symbol reference, cross-edge, aggregate, repo graph index, import reference, and external-symbol reference types |
46	| `internal/cli/workspace/graph_collect.go` | The four SQL collectors at `workspace.go:1217–1446`; callers continue to own validated database acquisition and closure |
47	| `internal/cli/workspace/graph_edges.go` | Cross-repo contract/import/route/GraphQL/channel/resource/symbol matching, ranking, sorting, and bounded edge selection at `workspace.go:1447–2427` |
48	| `internal/cli/workspace/graph_identity.go` | Stable cross-edge IDs, display paths, symbol display, and search score at `workspace.go:2939–3005` |
49	| `internal/cli/workspace/main_test.go` | `TestMain` using `clitest.PinXDGRoots` |
50	| `internal/cli/workspace/graph_edges_test.go`, `validate_test.go` | The existing independent tests, with the same assertions and fixtures |
51	| `internal/cli/workspace_config.go` | Per-invocation construction of workspace store dependencies; analogous to `entities_config.go` |
52	
53	The exact 68 function/type candidates and source locations are recorded in `../workspace-pr2-symbols.json`. Includes neither comments/blank lines nor constants in the 1,542-line estimate. Move the necessary workspace path/schema/display-name constants and the name-validation regexp with their readers. Keep one home for each value; export only values needed by remaining callers.
54	
55	### Code retained in CLI
56	
57	- Cobra command constructors and `runWorkspace*` orchestration remain in `workspace.go` for this PR. They call the new store/algorithm API directly; do not introduce a new package containing only command wrappers.
58	- Keep retrieval results, graph payloads/metrics, regression/review results, and their shared semantic/retrieval model types in CLI. Do not copy those models or move them into `base` merely to satisfy this extraction.
59	- Keep `workspaceSemanticSource`, freshness calculation, member checkout validation, graph-store opening, scan orchestration, and output publication checks in CLI.
60	- Keep `captureWorkspaceRetrievalPrivacyPolicies`, `captureWorkspaceDerivedReadPolicies`, and output revalidation in their existing orchestration paths.
61	- Keep `runSupervisedWatch`, `supervisedWatchLoop`, workspace watch orchestration, signal handling, daemon restart, and shared agent budget logic in CLI.
62	- Keep the generic `writeJSON`, `writeText`, `writeTextToWriter`, and `stickyErrorWriter` helpers in CLI. They happen to live in `workspace.go`, but many unrelated commands use them.
63	- Keep `workspaceFreshnessWarning`, `workspaceRepoBlockNeedsHeader`, and `splitWorkspaceID` in CLI: the first two belong to presentation; the last depends on shared retrieval source prefixes.
64	- Keep `workspace_patterns.go`, `pattern_workspace.go`, and `pattern_workspace_semantic.go` with their implementations and tests until the next boundary proposal.
65	
66	## Shared contracts and dependency injection
67	
68	Use workspace-owned exported models (`Manifest`, `Repo`, `RepoFreshness`, `AddResult`, and graph types). CLI type aliases are acceptable where they preserve existing integration tests and reduce mechanical churn. Do not create copied structs, forwarding functions, copied variables, or const aliases.
69	
70	The store must use the existing filesystem/security implementations through per-instance dependencies. A concrete shape to implement is:
71	
72	```go
73	type StoreDeps struct {
74	    DataDir              func(base.EntireEnv) (string, error)
75	    RejectRootPath       func(string, string) error
76	    RejectPathComponents func(string, string) error
77	    AcquireLock          func(string) (io.Closer, error)
78	    AtomicWrite          func(string, []byte, fs.FileMode) error
79	}
80	
81	type StoreConfig struct {
82	    Env               base.EntireEnv
83	    Deps              StoreDeps
84	    LegacyRepoDirName string
85	    LockDirName       string
86	}
87	```
88	
89	`workspaceStore(env)` in CLI constructs this configuration without resolving paths early. Its `DataDir` adapter invokes `resolvePluginDirs` at the same point the old operation did. Its lock adapter binds the existing `workspace_manifest_locked` error code and `brainWriteLockTimeout`. The path configuration receives the existing repo-store and lock-directory constants. Its atomic writer delegates to the original implementation with the original modes.
90	
91	Expose operations corresponding to the existing behavior: `Dir`, `DirOrEmpty`, `LoadManifest`, `WriteManifest`, `AddRepoLocked`, `AcquireManifestLock`, and `MergeRefreshResult`. Private implementation helpers remain private. Export only graph functions/types actually required by CLI callers; independent tests in package `workspace` can access the remaining private helpers.
92	
93	Important call-site examples:
94	
95	- `setup.go` calls `workspaceStore(env).AddRepoLocked(...)`; the read/modify/write transaction stays inside the store.
96	- MCP loads a workspace model through the store, applies its existing scope filtering, then calls the existing CLI graph/review/regression operation with that filtered manifest.
97	- Pattern code obtains a directory or manifest through the store but retains all existing privacy and publication checks.
98	- `runWorkspaceRemove` continues to hold the **same** manifest lock across load, mutation, write, or whole-workspace deletion. The lock remains outside the directory being deleted.
99	- Graph collectors receive the existing validated `*sql.DB`. Moving collection SQL does not authorize opening arbitrary graph paths in the new package.
100	
101	The Graph impact records show the manifest's consumers in MCP and pattern code and the store's consumers in setup. The generic output helpers have unrelated consumers across the CLI. These are ownership boundaries, not reasons to move those entire feature closures.
102	
103	## Test movement
104	
105	Move only the exact 33 roots in the appendix initially. These tests call the selected algorithms/validators directly and do not require the full CLI root or semantic/provider fixtures. Preserve test names, table cases, assertions, fixture data, and build tags. Allowed edits are package/import changes and symbol qualification needed by the move.
106	
107	Keep the following in CLI, mechanically updating calls to the new API:
108	
109	- `TestWorkspacePropagatesPluginDirErrors`: it verifies the real plugin resolver; replacing it with a fake dependency would weaken the test.
110	- Root command routes, malformed manifests, output failures, path/symlink protections, and legacy migration integration cases.
111	- All five concurrency tests, including `TestConcurrentWorkspaceAddsAllPersist` and `TestConcurrentSetupRegistrationsAllPersist`; they exercise the real lock and setup adapters.
112	- MCP sibling-scope and forged-checkout tests.
113	- Graph-store/cache, privacy, memory/watch, retrieval, regression/review, and pattern integration tests.
114	
115	Do not move integration tests to an external test package that imports `cli` and then count them as independently cached workspace tests. Do not replace real provider/storage fixtures with fakes simply to move a test. More tests can move only when their existing dependencies move intact, with the inventory and measurement updated explicitly.
116	
117	The test movement list is a source/Graph-backed plan, not a compile result. Compile the new package early. If a hidden dependency appears, resolve its actual ownership and update the move list explicitly; never silently omit the test or broaden the extraction into another subsystem.
118	
119	## Implementation sequence
120	
121	1. **Capture the baseline.** Start from current `origin/main` containing #486; record its commit, full runnable test/benchmark/example/fuzz inventory, pinned CLI `main_test.go` hash, and Windows harness settings. The supplied inventory and impact evidence are anchored to `0351e495`; refresh changed anchors if main advances. Do not rename the current branch automatically.
122	2. **Move the graph models and algorithms first.** Add the package and XDG-pinned `TestMain`, move the graph functions and 31 graph tests, qualify production callers, then compile/test CLI and workspace. This validates a boundary with no new filesystem behavior.
123	3. **Move workspace models and the store.** Add the five dependency adapters, move the two remaining validator/predicate tests, update setup/MCP/pattern/CLI callers, and preserve the exact operation order. Maintain a single home for constants and the regexp. No environment-resolution or lock implementation extraction is needed.
124	4. **Run focused integration tests.** Exercise the original scope/privacy, symlink/migration, setup registration, concurrent add/refresh/remove, graph cache, retrieval, and root-command tests against the new adapters. No assertion or expected-output changes should be needed.
125	5. **Verify the extraction mechanically.** Reconcile every runnable name across all packages; compare the moved test bodies after normalizing only package/import/qualified-name changes; confirm no reverse import or duplicate mutable variable; confirm the pinned root `main_test.go` hash is unchanged; run Graph diff for the moves.
126	6. **Run the full gates.** Format, build, vet, full race tests, Windows harness unit tests, and mutation checks. Commit with explicit paths, publish a PR, and require native Windows compile/inventory/shards/non-heavy execution/integrity to pass.
127	7. **Measure the actual benefit.** Capture before/after CLI and workspace compile/test durations with comparable cache conditions. Demonstrate independent workspace test caching using an actual temporary core-only source change, remove it, and verify a clean tree. Report the result without projecting the pattern-family timings onto this PR.
128	
129	## Verification commands and acceptance
130	
131	Use package concurrency one for the local full suite if disk pressure returns. The previous full local race run took 732.7 seconds and passed; maintain enough free space for compilation and fixtures.
132	
133	```sh
134	gofmt -l -s internal/cli
135	go build ./...
136	go vet ./...
137	go test -race ./internal/cli/workspace -count=1
138	go test -race -p=1 ./... -count=1 -timeout=30m
139	python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tools/ci-bench/windows-production/tests -p 'test_*.py'
140	python3 -B tools/coverage/mutation_check.py
141	```
142	
143	Select focused CLI tests from the unchanged inventory, including workspace, concurrent workspace/setup registration, and MCP workspace scope cases. The exact before/after runnable-name set must match, with 33 roots changing packages if the planned list compiles unchanged. Do not rely on equal counts alone, and do not count `TestMain` as a runnable test.
144	
145	No production Windows settings change is planned for this small, independently tested package. Verify that it is included exactly once in the existing non-heavy package path, removed roots no longer appear in CLI inventory, and stale weight entries remain harmless. Run `prepare.py` on native Windows CI; it is not a local macOS dry run. Do not change pinned declarations, shard settings, or weights merely to make validation pass.
146	
147	Acceptance requires all of the following:
148	
149	- New package owns the selected implementation, not wrappers calling back into CLI.
150	- No import cycle, mutable-variable copy, altered serialized shape, new skip, lost runnable root, or weakened assertion.
151	- Original scope, privacy, path safety, membership-lock, stable-ID/order, and output-error tests pass through the new API.
152	- Full local race validation and native Windows CI pass.
153	- PR description reports actual moved roots and measured compile/cache results; it makes no unsupported wall-clock speedup claim.
154	
155	## Following workspace stages
156	
157	The next performance-bearing candidate is the pattern-family implementation in `pattern_workspace.go` and `pattern_workspace_semantic.go`, with `workspace_patterns.go` orchestration considered separately. The six family tests account for the 67.35-second elapsed sum. Before scheduling that extraction, map the complete corpus/schema, SQLite safety, privacy publication, agent-runner, and test-fixture closures. The `twoRepoWorkspace` fixture builds real member corpora through shared pattern builders, so moving those tests is not a file rename.
158	
159	Retain root-command integration tests until their production seams and fixtures allow a move without replacing root coverage. Then reassess retrieval/graph orchestration and watch lifecycle as their own boundaries. Avoid promising a single follow-up PR for all three subsystems before their impacts are measured.
160	
161	CI package selection remains a separate follow-up. Coverage profiles disable ordinary Go result caching in the current workflow; this extraction alone does not implement affected-package selection or eliminate the full coverage run.
162	
163	## Evidence and analysis limits
164	
165	- Recorded constraints: Brain facts `792b23a8f15ba813bf730e72` and `09552bd5a25fd72416a35b5a`, retrieved in `../workspace-plan-recall.json`.
166	- Graph v0.5.0, full profile, committed source: `../workspace-plan-impact-index.json` indexes 145 per-symbol impact reports covering the workspace file's function/type/method surface. `../workspace-pr2-symbols.json` selects the proposed subset.
167	- Boundary edges: `../workspace-boundary-evidence.json`; test dependency evidence: `../workspace-test-dependencies.json`.
168	- Graph reported partial failures in non-Go runner/benchmark JSON, plus incomplete evidence for some data-flow edges. No Go parse failures were reported. Some cross-file names resolve heuristically; source inspection verified the store/MCP boundaries and rejected an apparent production dependency on a test-local variable named `repo`.
169	- The provider does not emit the workspace constants/regexp as symbol definitions in this snapshot. Impact lookups returned related-symbol suggestions rather than exact constant/regexp definitions. Their current literal/name uses were checked directly and recorded in `../workspace-plan-constant-uses.json`; recheck changed uses during implementation. Graph output is not proof of a complete identifier closure; compilation and exact inventories remain required.

1	# COR-2268 PR 1: foundation packages + entities extraction
2	
3	> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
4	
5	**Goal:** First extraction PR for COR-2268 — create the shared foundation packages and move the `entities` command cluster out of `internal/cli`, proving the whole split pipeline with CI green.
6	
7	**Architecture:** Three-layer DAG: `internal/cli` (root assembly + not-yet-extracted clusters) → `internal/cli/entities` (pilot feature package) → `internal/cli/internal/base` (shared prod helpers, incl. hook-seam vars). `internal/cli/internal/clitest` holds cross-package test support (XDG pin, shared fakes); test files only. Feature packages never import `internal/cli`; `internal/cli` imports feature packages.
8	
9	**Tech Stack:** Go 1.27.2, cobra, stdlib only. No new dependencies.
10	
11	**Spec:** Linear COR-2268 (https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2268). Dependency measurements: `.context/graph-symbols.ndjson`, `.context/graph-edges.ndjson` analysis summarized below.
12	
13	## Continuation notes (2026-10-24)
14	
15	Task 1 was already committed as 94ef9dad. Current implementation follows the three-layer DAG, with source-verified adjustments:
16	
17	- `main_test.go` calls `resolvePluginDirs` and the XDG constants directly. Moving all of env.go conflicts with both the frozen file and the no-forwarding-shims requirement. Move shared environment/storage types and retain environment resolution in cli.
18	- The concrete runner depends on Git hardening; manifest loading depends on source manifests, checkpoint formats, and migration logic. Keep those implementations in cli and inject per-invocation operations through `entities.Config` / `entities.Deps`.
19	- Move safe reads and their single-home bounds, path resolution, JSON/string helpers, checkpoint trailer parsing, GitScalar, fact locus helpers, and shared options/types into base.
20	- Extract entities commands, history/cache reads, refresh, and provenance. Retain storage/privacy/session adapters in cli. Keep integration tests that require private CLI fixtures in cli, as Task 3 permits. Move the independent provenance tie-break test and safe-read unit tests unchanged apart from names/imports.
21	- Exact runnable-name inventory: 3,459 before and after (includes benchmarks/examples/fuzz roots); no missing or added names. Pinned TestMain is byte-identical.
22	- `go build ./...`, focused tests, `go vet ./...`, race tests for entities/base/clitest, and all 41 Windows harness unit tests pass.
23	- Full non-race repository suite passes with package concurrency 1; all four mutation cases pass. The local full race run hit ENOSPC, but full macOS/Ubuntu race and coverage CI jobs pass. Native Windows compile/plan, race vet, all six shards, non-heavy packages, and final coverage/integrity verification pass.
24	- `prepare.py` is not a portable dry run: it requires a clean tracked checkout and GOOS=windows/GOARCH=amd64/CGO_ENABLED=1. Native Windows CI verified the actual inventory and partition.
25	- Fetched origin/main: PR #485 independently changed the harness to six shards and updated weights. This extraction does not modify the harness.
26	
27	- Rebased on origin/main and pushed commits `b1781911` (clitest) and `2f648d6a` (extraction). PR: https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/486. Repository CI is green. The isolated-cache demonstration passes: an actual core-only source addition reruns CLI tests while entities/base/clitest remain cached. Evidence: `.context/cache-demo.log`. Temporary probe and cache were removed. External Entire Gates/Partial Gates remain pending at preparation time.
28	
29	## Global Constraints
30	
31	- Tests are moved, not rewritten: same assertions, same fixtures (ticket acceptance).
32	- Do NOT modify `internal/cli/main_test.go` — its normalized source SHA-256 is pinned in `tools/ci-bench/windows-production/settings.json` (`expectedTestMainDeclarations`); any edit fails the Windows prepare job closed. PR 1 makes zero changes under `tools/ci-bench/`.
33	- Hook-seam vars (`defaultMaxReadBytes`, `maxManifestBytes`, …) get exactly ONE home. When one moves to `base`, every reader and every test that swaps it references `base.<Name>`. Never leave a `var old = base.New` shim for a VAR — swapping the shim would not affect base readers (split-brain). Function and const shims are forbidden too: sed-rename call sites instead.
34	- Type moves use aliases in `internal/cli` (`type Options = base.Options`) so `cmd/entire-brain/main.go` (the only external importer) and the ~200 unmoved files compile unchanged.
35	- Every new test package has a `main_test.go` whose `TestMain` calls `clitest.PinXDGRoots` — without it, tests write junk into the developer's real brain store (documented escape: 1,193 fallthroughs).
36	- Format gate before push: `gofmt -l -s` empty + `go vet ./...` (repo has no oxfmt binary; CI gates on these).
37	- Commits: explicit file names in `git add`, never `-A`/`.`. End messages with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
38	
39	## Review Focus
40

gh pr create --draft --base main --title "refactor(cli): extract session privacy state into brainstore (COR-2268)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Why

Continues the [COR-2268](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2268) `internal/cli` split. The six heavy workspace-family integration tests still depend on real privacy gates; this PR moves the privacy-state foundation those gates read so the gate layer itself can leave CLI next, and so `patterns`/`workspace` code can consume privacy state by import instead of injection.

## What moved (to `internal/cli/internal/brainstore`)

- **Versioned JSON state decoding**: `DecodeVersionedJSONBody`, `DecodeStrictVersionedJSON`, `CheckedVersionedJSONHeader`, `IsUnknownFieldError`, `ErrTrailingJSONData`.
- **Session tombstone state**: types, checked loader, save/marshal, `NormalizePrivacyTranscriptPath`.
- **Privacy transaction records**: type, Windows-safe filename escaping, rel path, write/load/decode, transcript-path recovery.
- **Brain-relative atomic write/remove**: `WriteBrainRelativeFileAtomic`, `RemoveBrainRelativeFile`.
- **Single-home constants**: `HistoryDirName`, `SessionsDirName`, `ConversationSessionIDPrefix`, `UnsupportedVersionCode`.

CLI keeps type aliases for the moved types; every function/const call site is renamed (no shims). The session read guard, derived-read gate, retrieval policy locking, and the full privacy verifier **stay in CLI** — the guard filters CLI retrieval models and the verifier needs the transcript store — they are the next boundary.

11 test roots move with their code (8 versioned-state decode, 3 privacy-transaction path-safety); bodies unchanged apart from package/import/qualified names. Two deliberate test edits: the CLI `DisallowUnknownFields` source-scan allowlist drops the moved shared-decoder entry, and one moved diagnostic string names the exported function.

## Validation

- Exact runnable-name inventory reconciles: 3497 → 3486 CLI, 23 → 34 brainstore, 3520 total unchanged; moved bodies verified identical under name normalization.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l -s` clean; `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` passes.
- Full local race suite (`-race -p=1 -count=1 ./...`): all 21 packages pass, zero failures.
- Focused CLI privacy/tombstone/manifest race tests pass (50.9s); all six extracted packages pass fresh race runs.
- All 41 Windows harness unit tests and all 4 mutation checks pass. `internal/cli/main_test.go` and `tools/ci-bench/` are untouched.

## Risks

- Windows plain-`go test` file-lock flake remains the watch item on the first Windows CI run of the grown `brainstore` package (no detached workers spawned; expected clean).
- Moved roots' shard weights fall back to `defaultWeightSeconds` by design.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

content.text:
In simple terms, [PR #510](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/510) removes a lock that has been blocking the whole refactoring effort.

**The background.** Every test in `internal/cli` relies on a safety net in `main_test.go`: before any test runs, it redirects the four XDG environment variables to a throwaway temp directory, so tests can never accidentally write into the real brain store under your home directory. Because this safety net is so important, the Windows CI harness holds a fingerprint (a SHA-256 hash) of that function and refuses to build if anyone changes the file. That made `main_test.go` effectively frozen.

**The problem.** The frozen file also happens to call `resolvePluginDirs` directly, which forces that function — and all of environment resolution — to stay inside the `cli` package forever. That's been the roadblock to moving the workspace test fixtures (and the ~67 seconds of heavy family integration tests) out of the giant `cli` package.

**What the PR does — three small things:**
1. Shrinks the frozen function to one line: `TestMain` now just calls `clitest.PinXDGRoots`, the identical shared copy of the safety net that every already-extracted package has been using since the split began. Two small helper tests move with it.
2. Updates the fingerprint in the Windows harness settings to match the new one-line function. I computed it with the harness's own tool, so it's exactly what Windows CI will compute.
3. Changes no behavior: same env vars pinned, same temp-dir scheme, and the one test that needs the *real* home directory back (the live end-to-end test) uses the shared helper — I ran it against the real installed provider and it passes.

**Why it matters.** With the freeze gone, `resolvePluginDirs` can finally move out of `cli`, which unlocks moving the workspace-pattern fixtures and heavy tests — the first step that actually shrinks the CLI test suite, which is the whole point of COR-2268.

content.text:
#517 validated on main (dead file gone, build/vet pass).

**Why small updates still re-run everything today** — two separate blockers:

1. **The coverage flag defeats Go's test cache.** The ubuntu/macos `test` job runs `tools/coverage/run.py --race` with `-coverprofile`, and Go never caches test results when coverage profiling is on. So even a perfectly split repo re-runs every package on every PR. The package split is *necessary* (selection is impossible with one package) but not *sufficient*.
2. **~97% of test roots still live in `internal/cli`** (3,479 of ~3,590). Any change touching core CLI re-runs that giant package regardless of caching, and a change to `base`/`brainstore` invalidates everything above them. Gains only show up when the touched package is leaf-like and the core is small.

**The path from here, in order:**

1. **Keep shrinking the core where the weight actually is** (per yesterday's fresh measurement): the refresh/transcript-ingestion subsystem (Refresh 86s + Fileless 47s — one closure around the transcript store and history projection), then Brief (25s), remaining Workspace commands (41s), History (20s). Semantic turned out to be light (10s) and drops in priority. Each extraction follows the now-proven recipe. Two or three more PRs gets the core's test time roughly halved.
2. **The CI selection PR** — the piece that directly answers your question. Two viable designs:
   - *Affected-package selection*: compute changed packages from the PR diff plus the `go list` reverse-dependency graph; run the coverage suite only on affected packages; keep the full run on merges to main and nightly. Deterministic, no cache infrastructure needed.
   - *Cache-based*: drop `-coverprofile` on PR runs (move full coverage to nightly/main) and persist `GOCACHE` across CI runs so Go's own test cache skips untouched packages.
   
   I'd do affected-package selection — it also lets the **Windows harness** skip the heavy `cli.test.exe` compile entirely when a PR only touches a leaf package, and that `-race` compile (~7 min on Windows) is the recorded wall-clock hog.
3. **Rebalance and measure** — the ticket's acceptance step: 6–8 packages of comparable weight, then demonstrate a leaf-package PR skipping the rest and record the actual before/after CI wall-clock.

**Realistic end state** (from the original estimate, still valid): a PR touching one sub-package goes from the current ~8-minute floor to ~4–5 minutes; a PR touching `base`/`brainstore` still pays full price — gains scale with how leaf-like the change is.

**Recommended next step**: scope and implement the refresh/transcript extraction (biggest remaining weight), then do the CI selection PR — selection could even come first since it pays off immediately for the already-extracted packages. Say which order you want, or "keep going" and I'll take refresh next.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the full Go suite and instrumented binary contracts, retaining failures."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import platform
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]


def capture(*args):
    return subprocess.check_output(args, cwd=ROOT, text=True).strip()


def binary_contracts(binary, output, cgo, counters):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="brain-binary-contract-") as temporary:
        directory = Path(temporary)
        env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith(("ENTIRE_", "GIT_", "XDG_"))}
        env.update({key: str(directory / key) for key in (
            "HOME", "USERPROFILE", "APPDATA", "LOCALAPPDATA",
            "XDG_CONFIG_HOME", "XDG_DATA_HOME", "XDG_STATE_HOME", "XDG_CACHE_HOME"
        )})
        env["GOCOVERDIR"] = str(counters)
        cases = [("help", ["--help"], 0), ("version", ["version"], 0),
                 ("capabilities", ["capabilities", "--json"], 0),
                 ("invalid-command", ["not-a-brain-command"], 1)]
        for name, args, expected in cases:
            result = subprocess.run([str(binary), *args], cwd=directory, env=env,
                                    capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
            (output / f"binary-{name}.json").write_text(json.dumps({
                "args": args, "exit_code": result.returncode,
                "stdout": result.stdout, "stderr": result.stderr,
            }, indent=2))
            if result.returncode != expected:
                raise RuntimeError(f"{name}: exit {result.returncode}, expected {expected}: {result.stderr}")
            if name == "help" and "Usage:" not in result.stdout:
                raise RuntimeError("missing CLI usage")
            if name == "version" and result.stdout.strip() != "dev":
                raise RuntimeError("unexpected unstamped version")
            if name == "invalid-command" and "unknown command" not in result.stderr:
                raise RuntimeError("missing invalid-command diagnostic")
            if name == "capabilities":
                capabilities = json.loads(result.stdout)
                if capabilities["schema_version"] != 1 or capabilities["build"]["brain_cgo"] != cgo:
                    raise RuntimeError("binary capabilities disagree with build")
        # These metadata commands must not initialize repository or user state.
        if list(directory.iterdir()):
            raise RuntimeError("read-only binary contracts created persistent state")

import json
import pathlib
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

TOOL = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "affected.py"
ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
MODULE = "github.com/entireio/entire-brain"


def run_tool(file_names):
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".txt", delete=False) as handle:
        handle.write("\n".join(file_names) + "\n")
        listing = handle.name
    try:
        output = subprocess.check_output(
            [sys.executable, "-B", str(TOOL), "--changed-files", listing],
            cwd=ROOT,
            text=True,
        )
    finally:
        pathlib.Path(listing).unlink()
    return json.loads(output)


class AffectedSelectionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_non_go_change_selects_the_full_suite(self):
        decision = run_tool(["tools/coverage/run.py"])
        self.assertEqual(decision["mode"], "full")

    def test_module_file_change_selects_the_full_suite(self):
        decision = run_tool(["go.mod"])
        self.assertEqual(decision["mode"], "full")

    def test_empty_change_set_selects_nothing(self):
        decision = run_tool([])
        self.assertEqual(decision["mode"], "none")

    def test_go_file_outside_every_package_selects_the_full_suite(self):
        decision = run_tool(["no/such/dir/x.go"])
        self.assertEqual(decision["mode"], "full")

    def test_leaf_package_change_includes_its_importers(self):
        decision = run_tool(["internal/cli/patterns/corpus_access.go"])
        self.assertEqual(decision["mode"], "selected")
        packages = set(decision["packages"])
        self.assertIn(MODULE + "/internal/cli/patterns", packages)
        # cli imports patterns, and the main module wires the cli root command,
        # so both must re-run when patterns changes.
        self.assertIn(MODULE + "/internal/cli", packages)

    def test_top_package_change_excludes_packages_it_does_not_reach(self):
        decision = run_tool(["internal/cli/root.go"])
        self.assertEqual(decision["mode"], "selected")
        packages = set(decision["packages"])
        self.assertIn(MODULE + "/internal/cli", packages)
        # Nothing in cli is imported by the leaf helper packages, so a cli-only
        # change must not re-run them.
        self.assertNotIn(MODULE + "/internal/cli/patterns", packages)
        self.assertNotIn(MODULE + "/internal/cli/internal/base", packages)

    def test_test_only_dependency_affects_its_test_importers(self):
        decision = run_tool(["internal/cli/internal/clitest/clitest.go"])
        self.assertEqual(decision["mode"], "selected")
        packages = set(decision["packages"])
        # clitest is imported only by _test.go files; test imports must still
        # count as affectedness or moved pins would silently stop re-running.
        self.assertIn(MODULE + "/internal/cli", packages)
        self.assertIn(MODULE + "/internal/cli/patterns", packages)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # Depth 2 exposes the PR merge commit's first parent (the base tip),
          # which package selection diffs against. Pushes ignore the extra depth.
          fetch-depth: 2
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af
        with: { go-version: "1.27.2" }
      # Pull requests run only the packages the diff can affect (reverse import
      # closure, including test imports) with -race and WITHOUT coverage
      # profiling: -coverprofile disables Go's test caching and adds atomic
      # counter overhead, and PR coverage artifacts were informational only.
      # Any non-.go change falls back to the full coverage run below. Pushes to
      # main always run the complete coverage suite, so merged evidence is
      # unchanged.
      - name: Select affected packages (pull requests)
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        id: affected
        run: |
          python3 -B tools/coverage/affected.py --base HEAD^1 --head HEAD > "$RUNNER_TEMP/affected.json"
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/affected.json"
          python3 -B -c '
          import json, sys
          decision = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
          print("mode=" + decision["mode"])
          print("packages=" + " ".join(decision.get("packages", [])))
          ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/affected.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Test affected packages with race
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && steps.affected.outputs.mode == 'selected'
        run: go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30m ${{ steps.affected.outputs.packages }}
      - name: Measure instrumented CLI contracts without the full suite
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && steps.affected.outputs.mode != 'full'
        run: python3 -B tools/coverage/run.py --race --binary-only --output "${{ runner.temp }}/brain-coverage"
      - name: Test with coverage and binary contracts
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || steps.affected.outputs.mode == 'full'
        run: python3 -B tools/coverage/run.py --race --output "${{ runner.temp }}/brain-coverage"

          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/brain-coverage/*.json
            ${{ runner.temp }}/brain-coverage/*.jsonl
            ${{ runner.temp }}/brain-coverage/*.out

def changed_files(base, head, cwd=ROOT):
    # --no-renames keeps a rename visible as an add plus a delete, so a .go
    # file moved between packages marks BOTH packages as changed. With rename
    # detection, --name-only lists only the destination and the source package
    # would silently keep its stale selection.
    output = subprocess.check_output(
        ["git", "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", f"{base}", f"{head}"],
        cwd=cwd,
        text=True,
    )
    return [line for line in output.splitlines() if line.strip()]

### What landed (2026-10-25 → 2026-10-26)

Twelve PRs, all merged, full race suite green on every one:

- **Payoff**: #516 (workspace pattern corpus + families → patterns, including all six heavy family integration tests; 10 roots moved). #517 cleanup.
- **CI selection**: #518 — PRs run only diff-affected packages (reverse import closure incl. test imports) with `-race` and no coverage; non-Go changes fail safe to the full coverage run; pushes to main unchanged.
- **#519**: fixture refreshes were executing the real `codex` binary on dev machines (~69s per suite run, real agent spend; invisible on CI where no agent is installed). Fixed with fail-fast PATH shims; 69s → 0.5s. Likely the cause of the long-standing "local cli suite times out" baseline.

### Acceptance status

- "PR touching one sub-package demonstrably skips the others" — **met**, demonstrated live: #519's CI run selected `{cmd/entire-brain, internal/cli}` and skipped every extracted package. ubuntu test job 3m23s (was ~4.0–4.4m).
- "green with -race on all three OSes" — **holds** on every PR; Windows verify green throughout, shard plan covers moved roots correctly (weights fall back by design).
- "tests moved not rewritten" — **held**: every moved root byte-compared under a mechanical rename map; inventories reconciled exactly on every PR (currently 3,479 cli / 32 patterns / 34 brainstore / 18 base / others).
- "6–8 packages of comparable test weight" — **not met**: cli still holds ~97% of roots. See below for why the original target needs revisiting.

### What the fresh measurement changed

Full `-race` per-test timing at current main (3,444 roots, 561s elapsed sum):

- The ticket's suggested boundaries no longer match the weight. `semantic` (~254 tests suggested) is now 130 roots at **9.7s**. The heavy groups are refresh/ingestion (86s — but 69s of that was the #519 agent-exec bug, now gone), transcript-fileless (47s), remaining workspace commands (41s), brief (25s).
- The remaining heavy tests are mostly **root-command integration** (full `refresh`/export runs over real git fixtures) plus two legitimate singles (mcp deadline-observation 20s, fileless export matrix 19s). The workspace extraction showed this class does not relocate: implementations move, root-command tests stay in cli.
- Because cli imports every extracted package, **every Go PR still re-runs the cli suite (147s on CI)**. Selection pays off fully only for the leaf packages, and the Windows ~8-minute floor is untouched by selection for the same reason.

### Remaining options, by value

1. **Keep extracting** (refresh/transcript store, brief, history): shrinks cli's compile unit (helps the Windows `-race` compile, the recorded wall-clock hog) and moves what unit-level weight exists, but the per-PR gain per extraction is now smaller than the landed ones.

3. **Root-command test cost**: the remaining big wins would come from cheaper integration fixtures or splitting command assembly itself (cli stops being the universal importer). Larger design change; not in the original ticket scope.

Honest answer: **partially — the mechanism is real and proven live, but the magnitude is limited by the repo's shape.**

**What you actually got:**
- On #519 (a one-file test change), CI genuinely ran only 2 packages instead of the whole module — the log shows `{"mode": "selected", "packages": [cmd/entire-brain, internal/cli]}` and every extracted package (patterns, brainstore, workspace, entities, base…) was skipped, coverage instrumentation dropped. The ubuntu test job went from the historical ~4.0–4.4 min to **3m23s**.
- Locally the win is bigger: extracted packages now cache across runs, and the suite no longer secretly executes the real `codex` agent (~70s + real API spend per run, fixed in #519).

**What you didn't get — and why:** I just probed four true leaf packages (`factmerge`, `apiurl`, `brainwire`, `agentsetup`), and every one of their reverse-import closures **still contains `internal/cli`** — because cli imports essentially everything to assemble the root command. So there is currently *no possible Go change* that skips the cli suite, and the cli suite is 147s of the job. Likewise the Windows chain (~8 min, the real floor) compiles and shards cli on every PR regardless of selection.

So the before/after for a typical small Go change:

| | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| ubuntu/macos test job | ~4.0–4.4 min (everything + coverage) | ~3.4–4.1 min (cli closure only, no coverage) |
| Extracted packages | always re-run | **skipped unless touched** |
| Windows chain | ~8 min | ~8 min (unchanged) |
| Local full suite | timeouts, real agent runs | ~70s faster, hermetic |

The remaining gap is structural, not mechanical: as long as `internal/cli` is both 97% of the tests and the universal importer, every change pays it. Closing that gap means either continuing to move test weight out of cli (diminishing per-PR returns, as the measurement showed) or the bigger step the original ticket didn't scope — splitting command assembly so cli stops being one giant package that imports the world. That's the decision now sitting in the Linear comment.

what do you mean splitting command assembly?

Today, `internal/cli` is really two things fused into one package:

```
cmd/entire-brain ──> internal/cli ──────────────> patterns, workspace, entities,
                     │                            brainstore, base, …
                     ├─ NewRootCommand()          (the extracted leaves)
                     ├─ refresh: command + implementation + tests
                     ├─ brief:   command + implementation + tests
                     ├─ privacy, seed, mcp, viz, dash, get, …
                     └─ 3,479 test roots
```

The **assembly** (building the cobra root, mounting subcommands, wiring `Options`) and the **feature implementations** live in the same package. That's why cli is simultaneously 97% of the tests *and* in every package's reverse-import closure — any change anywhere re-runs it.

**Splitting command assembly** means inverting the top of that graph:

```
cmd/entire-brain ──> internal/cli (thin assembler, ~zero tests)
                        ├──> refreshcmd.New(opts)   + refresh tests
                        ├──> briefcmd.New(opts)     + brief tests
                        ├──> privacycmd.New(opts)   + privacy tests
                        ├──> workspacecmd.New(opts) + workspace command tests
                        └──> …
                     each of those ──> patterns / brainstore / base / …
```

Each feature package exports its own cobra command constructor; the root package just imports them and mounts them. The crucial consequence: the universal importer still exists, but it's **nearly test-free** — so being in every closure costs nothing. A change to brief re-runs `briefcmd` (~25s of tests) plus an empty assembler, not 147 seconds of everything. Windows stops having one giant `-race` compile unit, and the bespoke 8-shard harness can likely shrink toward plain per-package `go test`.

This is actually what the original ticket sketched ("6–8 packages: mcp, workspace, distill, brief…"); the twelve PRs so far built the basement that makes it possible (shared helpers, privacy gates, env resolution, test pins all have importable homes now).

**Why it's the expensive option — the honest costs:**

1. **Cross-command calls.** Commands reach into each other's internals today (refresh runs seed, workspace calls pattern surfaces, get/brief/mcp share the retrieval pipeline). Every shared helper needs a home package — same discipline as the last twelve PRs, but applied to the remaining 97%.
2. **`mcp.go` is a second hub** — it calls across nearly every feature. It either becomes its own big package (fine) or needs interfaces.
3. **The moved-not-rewritten rule bends slightly.** Root-integration tests that run `cmd.SetArgs(["refresh", …])` through the full root would re-point at `refreshcmd.New(...)` instead of `NewRootCommand(...)` — a one-line, principled change, but a change; a small set of genuinely cross-command tests stays with the assembler.
4. **Windows harness per package** — heavy-list entries and TestMain pins per new package, or a deliberate decision to retire sharding once no package is heavy. We've already done this dance once (#510), so it's known territory.

Rough shape if you fund it: one pilot PR per command cluster, starting with the most self-contained one (brief or viz) to validate the recipe, then the heavy ones (refresh/export, workspace commands, mcp) — probably 6–10 PRs of the same size as the recent ones. End state is the actual dream: a one-command change runs that command's tests in seconds, on every OS.

No action needed from me now — happy to scope the pilot (exact first cluster, its closure, and what the re-pointed tests look like) whenever you've thought it over.

Verified and recorded (Brain + a Linear addendum on COR-2268). What the MCP removal changes for the decision you're sitting on:

- **CLI shrank for free**: 3,479 → 3,225 test roots, and the 19.9s mcp-deadline single went with it. I validated main — build and vet are green.
- **The command-assembly split just got meaningfully cheaper.** Of the four costs I listed, #2 (`mcp.go` as a second hub calling into every feature) is simply gone. What remains is one hub — the thin root assembler, which would carry near-zero tests — plus the two real costs: finding homes for cross-command shared helpers (the same discipline as the last twelve PRs) and re-pointing root-integration tests from `NewRootCommand` to per-feature command constructors.

So the split option you're thinking over now looks like: ~6–9 bounded PRs (brief/viz pilot first, then refresh/export, workspace commands, privacy/sessions, history/get, seed/distill), with the known-hard part being the shared retrieval pipeline that get/brief share. The payoff stands: a one-command change runs that command's tests in seconds on every OS, and the Windows 8-shard harness likely retires once no single package is heavy.

No action from me until you've decided — the ticket now has the up-to-date numbers and the sharpened cost/benefit for that call.
do you think it's owrth it?

Yes — with one qualifier about how to buy it.

**The case for:** the payoff isn't just CI minutes, it's three compounding things:

1. **The per-PR floor actually falls.** Typical change today: ~4 min ubuntu/macos + ~8 min Windows, every time. After the split, a one-command change runs that command's package (seconds–30s) plus a near-empty assembler; and Windows' real cost — the ~3-minute `-race` compile of one giant package plus 6 shards — dissolves into medium packages that plain `go test` can parallelize. Plausible end state is ~3–4 min total, mostly fixed overhead. At this repo's PR velocity (I count ~20 merged PRs this weekend), that's hours of wall-clock and compute weekly, forever.
2. **The local dev loop is the bigger win.** Right now touching brief means re-running a 10+ minute package locally (the recorded "local suite times out" baseline, and until yesterday it also secretly ran a real agent). After the split it's `go test ./internal/cli/briefcmd` in seconds. That's friction every engineer pays daily.
3. **You get to delete the Windows sharding harness.** `tools/ci-bench` is a bespoke, fail-closed system that taxes every structural change (we paid that tax in #510). Once no package is "heavy," it retires. Deleting maintained machinery is worth more than the minutes.

**The case against is mostly gone.** The MCP removal killed the second hub; the twelve landed PRs already built the hard substrate (shared helpers, privacy seams, env resolution, test pins all have homes); the verification recipe (inventory reconciliation, normalized body comparison, race gates) is proven and catches loss. The genuinely uncertain part is one area: the shared retrieval pipeline behind `get`/`brief`, plus the judgment calls on re-pointing root-integration tests.

**The qualifier:** don't commit to all ~6–9 PRs up front. Fund **one pilot** — `viz` or `brief`, the most self-contained cluster — as a single PR. It validates the recipe on the new shape (command constructor, re-pointed tests, Windows handling) and gives you a measured number for what a per-command package actually costs and saves. If the pilot's numbers look like the projection, the rest is mechanical and can proceed at whatever pace suits; if the retrieval coupling turns out nastier than expected, you've spent one PR learning that instead of six.

So: worth it, pilot-first, and I'd pick `brief` as the pilot since it also carries real test weight (25s) that moves on day one.
is this idiomatic go in terms of repo structure?

Yes — it's not just idiomatic, it's the standard shape for every large Go CLI you'd name as a reference:

- **The Go toolchain itself**: `cmd/go/internal/{build,get,mod,run,test,...}` — each subcommand is its own internal package exposing a `*base.Command`, and `cmd/go/main.go` is a thin assembler that just registers them. This is the canonical example.
- **GitHub's `gh`**: `pkg/cmd/{pr,issue,repo,...}`, each package exporting `NewCmdPR(f *cmdutil.Factory)` with its own tests beside it; the `Factory` struct injects IO, config, and clients — almost exactly our `Options{Env, Runner, Now}` pattern, which means the dependency-injection style we've already built is the one this structure expects.
- **kubectl**: `pkg/cmd/{get,apply,delete,...}`, one package per command, assembled in `pkg/cmd/cmd.go`.
- **Docker CLI**: `cli/command/{container,image,network,...}`.

The current shape — one giant package holding every command plus its implementation — is the counter-pattern. Terraform's `internal/command` is the big-package example in the wild, and it suffers exactly the symptoms this ticket opened with (huge compile unit, no package-level test parallelism or caching).

Two idiom notes for the pilot, if it happens:

1. **Naming**: Go style prefers short, lower-case package names without stutter. The exemplars use a `cmd`/`command` parent directory with the feature as the package name — so `internal/cli/command/brief` (package `brief`) reads better than `briefcmd`. Since we already use `internal/cli/...` as the tree, something like `internal/cli/command/{brief,refresh,workspace,...}` fits what exists.
2. **What we already have is the unusual part, and it's fine**: the double-internal (`internal/cli/internal/base`) is legal and does its job (helpers invisible outside the cli tree), but it's rarer in the wild than a flat `internal/{base,brainstore,...}`. Not worth churning now — just don't deepen it further.

So structurally, the split moves the repo *toward* ecosystem norms, not away from them. The only non-idiomatic risk would be overdoing injection — `gh`'s Factory works because it stays small; if a command package ever needs a 15-field deps struct, that's a sign the helper belongs in a shared package instead.

# Command-assembly split — per-cluster recipe

Project trail: https://entire.com/gh/entireio/-/trails/2619 (one change per cluster).
Base branch for all wave-1 work: `cor-2268-cmdutil` (adds `internal/cli/internal/cmdutil` with WriteJSON/WriteText/WriteTextToWriter/StickyErrorWriter — use these, never copy them).

## Goal per cluster

Move one command cluster out of package `cli` into `internal/cli/command/<name>`
(package `<name>`), exporting `New(opts base.Options) *cobra.Command` (plus
additional constructors if the cluster registers several commands). The root
assembler (`internal/cli/root.go`) imports the package and mounts the command;
nothing else in `cli` may import the new package unless it already called the
moved code. The new package must NOT import `internal/cli`.

## Layering (already in place — use it, do not re-create it)

- `internal/cli/internal/base` — env/XDG/store paths (`base.EntireEnv`,
  `base.Options`, `base.ResolvePluginDirs`, `base.BrainDirForKey`), redaction,
  safe reads, agent args. `cli.Options`/`cli.EntireEnv` are aliases of these.
- `internal/cli/internal/brainstore` — locks, atomic writes, privacy state
  (tombstones, transactions, read guard, retrieval policy), untrusted state
  readers, error-code taxonomy (`brainstore.MemoryErrorCode`, `*Code` consts).
- `internal/cli/internal/cmdutil` — command output helpers.
- `internal/cli/internal/clitest` — `clitest.PinXDGRoots` (every new test
  package MUST have `main_test.go` with `func TestMain(m *testing.M) { os.Exit(clitest.PinXDGRoots(m)) }`),
  `clitest.UseHostXDGDataHome`, shared fakes.
